items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: Barney Begard and Omar Simeon. Omar Simeon, he was in Chicago. And those were, we were the four major students of Tio.

ctx.x: And I'm Dick Allen, and Lars Edergren is coming later. He's busy eating breakfast. Let's see, today is June the 20th, what's the date? 26th. 26th, 1972, and we're at 931 Charlotte Street, Lars Edergren's apartment. Oh, one of the things that, you remember Alan Ward, who's a friend of Mike Casimir, he was telling me that you took lessons from Tio? That's right, Lorenzo Tio. Who else would be there at the lessons at the same time? Did you meet any other musicians?
Yeah, yeah. Jimmy Noon was ahead of me. I was second, and Barney Begard and Omar Simeon. Omar Simeon, he was in Chicago. And those were, we were the four major students of Tio.

items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: And then formed a little group of my own. With Barney B. Godd on tenor we were learning in Saxton.

ctx.x: Can you tell us something about your training and taking lessons and so on?

Well, I started taking lessons around 9 years of age with my uncle, Wooden Joe Nicholas. He was my big influence on this jazz scene. And later on, I went to Papa Teo and took lessons with him for about a couple of years. Then Lorenzo Teo, his son. And finished up with him until around 1915. Then I started to go pro. My first gigs around New Orleans was with the Maple Leaf Band. Then Buddy Petite's Band. When Jimmy Noon left to go to Chicago, I played with Buddy Petite and several other bands around New Orleans.…
